Hi @Zoeeeeey ,

I tried on Colab and getting crash due to Low Memory resource.

`2024-03-20 09:41:37.338368: W tensorflow/tsl/framework/cpu_allocator_impl.cc:83] Allocation of 14391421936 exceeds 10% of free system memory.`

Could you please confirm your RAM size and also could you please test with latest TF version i.e TF2.16v.Since it is possible that few bugs might resolved in latest releases and thus saves our time.

It seems there is integer overflow happening with UnsortedSegmentSum Op which internally being used by `tf.math.unsorted_segment_mean`. Repro code snippet below & reference [gist](https://colab.sandbox.google.com/gist/SuryanarayanaY/2e15ecd56d841426985cfa84f873efdd/64023.ipynb#scrollTo=_oF8wIpuQptx).

```
data=tf.constant(value=np.random.randint(0,100,size=(3, 2)), shape=(3, 2), dtype=tf.int32)
segment_ids=3
segment_ids = tf.convert_to_tensor(segment_ids)
num_segments=3597855484

tf.raw_ops.UnsortedSegmentSum(data=data, segment_ids=segment_ids, num_segments=num_segments)
```

Hi, thank you for your explanation. 
In addition, I upgraded the version of TensorFlow and made some attempts, and this issue showed some different behaviors. 
Actually, I want to ask, does the code hint `Aborted (core dumped)` indicate that this is a bug in the current version?
@SuryanarayanaY

This must be a check fail that needs to be fixed with proper exception.

Anyways the overflow problem as mentioned in above [comment](https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/issues/64023#issuecomment-2009366453) might needs fix.

issue.title: Fix segment reduction overflow.

repository.name: tensorflow
repository.description: An Open Source Machine Learning Framework for Everyone

issue.body:
Fix segment reduction overflow.

The `nsegments` argument type must be the same as the `segment_ids`
(since the latter are just indices into `nsegments`).  For large
inputs that would overflow `Index` (`long`) but still fit into `int64_t`,
this was previously causing a uncaught failure, since it would pass
the validation checks that used `int64_t`, but then would result in
a negative value when it's actually used.

Fixes #64023.
